goal: A child's hand taps on the wall of the book corner, so the child sees the tapping.
mustShow: the hand taps on the wall
colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 shows the boy Sam: the four 3D views at the bottom are the approved character, and the flat drawing at the top is only a hint, so copy the 3D look; ignore the gray background, the labels, and the shadow. Picture 2 is the empty book corner of the kindergarten classroom: cream plaster walls with dark-brown timber beams, a light wooden floor, ONE big round wicker basket full of colorful picture books at the left, ONE big cream paper map with a blue river, a green hill, and a small red house on the wall, and ONE wooden toy kitchen at the right with a small RED toy pan on its cooker; use it as the background and keep the same corner. Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body. Hands are small, clean hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye, and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; no character here has an eyelash flick. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. The ears are smooth, with one clean rounded rim. Each piece of clothing is one even color with no pale patches, no pale blotches at the shoulders, and no stains. Do not change anyone's skin tone, hair, or clothes. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Sam: a five-year-old boy with a chibi look (a big head and a small body), short brown hair with a side-swept fringe, big brown eyes, a big open-mouth smile, a red T-shirt with two white stripes across the chest, blue shorts, blue shoes. The picture: a child's hand taps on the wall. A close shot at the wall, in the book corner (picture 2), from the other side of the room. The cream plaster wall fills the middle of the picture. Sam stands at the right of the picture, seen from the side, and he raises ONE hand and taps the wall with the flat side of his index finger: the fingertips touch the wall, and the hand is clearly in front of the wall, at about the height of his shoulder. The hand and the arm are big in the picture, and the tapping hand is the MAIN thing: the fingertips touch the wall and the hand is in the clear, with no basket, no map, and no other object in front of it. The wall shows one small round soft dent under the fingertips, so the reader sees the tap. His other arm hangs relaxed. The basket of books, the map, and the toy kitchen stay in the background, soft and simple. Exactly one boy and one hand. No puppy, no tail, and no other person. The page text is "Tap, tap, tap!" and is context only: do not draw any text. Exactly the characters named here are in the picture, and no other person or animal. A character of the pictures that this description does not name must not appear. Every named character has a clear, whole, friendly face. THE TAP: the fingertips of the raised hand touch the wall. The hand is not in the air and not on a basket, and the wall is not empty next to the hand.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, the cuffs, the buttons, and the stripes. No wrinkle lines on any face. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the floor line, the wall lines, each timber beam as one closed band, the basket as one closed shape with its books as a few big closed rectangles, the map as one closed rectangle with its river, its hill, and its house as closed shapes, the toy kitchen as one closed box shape with its shelf and its oven door as closed shapes, the red pan as one closed shape with one closed handle). No wood grain lines, no floor plank lines, no basket weave lines, no wall texture, no hatching, no tick marks, no small details. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes. Sam keeps his two white T-shirt stripes: draw each stripe as one closed band shape across the chest; each sleeve, the collar, the shorts, and each shoe are closed shapes. Each hand is one closed outline with five fingers drawn as separate rounded closed shapes (four fingers and one thumb). The tapping fingertips touch the wall line.
